subsystems.name: Unit-cell resonators
subsystems.role: the repeating element, smaller than the wavelength, that gives the material its unnatural optical response.
parts: phase-change or liquid-crystal inclusions for tuning

subsystems.name: Substrate and cladding
subsystems.role: mechanically supports the nanostructure and sets the surrounding optical index.

subsystems.name: Design and simulation stack
subsystems.role: computes which arrangement of unit cells produces the wanted wavefront.

subsystems.name: Patterning and etching
subsystems.role: turns the design into nanoscale features.

subsystems.name: Metrology
subsystems.role: verifies feature shape and optical performance.

subsystems.name: Tuning and control
subsystems.role: changes the optical response after fabrication.

buildSteps.title: Set the target response
buildSteps.detail: Start from the wavefront, lens or spectral filter wanted, then work out the phase and amplitude each unit cell must impart.

buildSteps.title: Design the unit cell
buildSteps.detail: Simulate candidate nanopillars across their height, diameter and spacing until their phase covers the full 0–2π range at the operating wavelength.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the array
buildSteps.detail: Place individual cells, often millions per square centimetre, in a pattern that builds the desired wavefront across the aperture.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate a mask or master
buildSteps.detail: Electron-beam lithography writes the pattern in resist; for high volume the pattern is transferred to a master stamp.

buildSteps.title: Replicate at scale
buildSteps.detail: Nanoimprint or deep-UV lithography copies the pattern, followed by deposition and plasma etching to carve the pillars.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: A protective layer or polymer fill is added to protect fragile features less than a micrometre tall.

buildSteps.title: Measure and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Optical and electron microscopy compare real performance with simulation, and the design is corrected.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a device
buildSteps.detail: The metasurface is aligned and bonded onto an image sensor, fibre tip or laser, and its driver electronics connected if it is tunable.

prerequisites.why: features must be far smaller than the wavelength — tens of nanometres at visible light.
silicon, titanium dioxide and gallium nitride bend light strongly enough in thin layers.
no closed-form recipe exists; every device is computed.
electron-beam writing is too slow for consumer volumes, so imprint and deep-UV routes matter.
switchable metasurfaces are held back by optical loss and slow switching.

pathway.milestone: metalenses and flat filters in research and early products
pathway.unlocks: thin, lightweight optics for cameras, phone sensors and augmented-reality glasses.
beam steering without moving parts, useful for LiDAR and free-space optical links.

pathway.milestone: apertures large enough for telescopes and microscopy
pathway.unlocks: diffraction-limited flat optics, if patterning and efficiency improve.
